extraction.Name: Sarah Douville
extraction.Refused/Protested: I told the Superintendent that I did not want the patent at the time when the names were being sent to Washington for the issuance of patents. But he said that we were able to make a living and would be better off with our patents. I did not make a protest after the patent came as I though it no use.
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: traded it to my son John Conoyer for his quarter that he got a patent to without asking for it; then sold that for $5000.00 the best I remember
extraction.Occupation/Income: My husband and son farms and I do what I can.
extraction.NOTES: Traded original allotment quarter to son John Conoyer in exchange for his quarter (which he also received a patent to without asking for it); subsequently sold that quarter for $5000.00. Not in good health lately. Has grown children; a grandchild stays with her as her mother is dead. States she did not ask for the patent and would like the land back; says she is too old to work and has some grandchildren to look after. Sworn before Jas. W. Cross, Notary Public, commission expires 4-28-32, on May 2, 1929.
